ceiling_directive: Determine the low-noise minimax pool complexity on the stated exact-budget model class by proving a matching adaptive sparse-exploration converse and an attaining recovery-valid design.
improvement_directive: Resolve the degree-one low-noise case first by constructing a fixed-budget separating design attaining the existing lower scale \(\max\{\log n,1/q\}\), or prove a stronger adaptive lower bound that rules out this scale; then propagate the identified sparse-exploration mechanism to general \(s\).
critique: The note proves an identification characterization, recovery upper bounds, and a minimax sample-complexity match only when \(\sigma^2/\delta^2\ge s+1\); outside that regime the sparse-exploration dependence remains unresolved. Consequently, the advertised “frontier” is presently a bracket whose noiseless and low-noise bounds can differ substantially, including a multiplicative gap between the degree-one random-pool upper bound and the proved \(\max\{\log n,1/q\}\) obstruction. The broader project objective involving cumulative welfare regret, top-\(B\) optimization, TATE inference, and selection-uniform edge inference is not defined or proved in the delivered note, which instead changes the object to graph-recovery pool complexity. Both attaining decoders also rely on exact optimizers or externally supplied optimization certificates, with no proved polynomial-time finite-precision procedure.
